96K likes, 2,423 comments - drmarkhyman on August 21, 2025: "New data just dropped: only 54% of Americans drink alcohol now - the LOWEST rate in 90 years.

That’s a 13-point crash in just 3 years. Something massive is happening, and if you’ve been questioning your relationship with alcohol, you’re part of a historic health revolution.

Here’s what’s driving this seismic shift:
- Young adults are leading with remarkable clarity - only 50% drink now (down from 72% in 2004).
- Women are stepping back in record numbers - down 11 points in just one year.
- Even drinkers are drinking dramatically less - only 24% had alcohol yesterday (record low), and the average is just 2.8 drinks per week.

As a doctor, I’ll say it clearly: No amount of alcohol is safe for human health. The idea that moderate drinking has benefits was based on flawed research. We now know alcohol causes 100,000+ cancer cases yearly and 20,000 preventable deaths.

Your liver processes alcohol as a toxin because that’s exactly what it is.

If you do choose to drink occasionally, see my other post on minimizing damage. But know this: 53% of Americans now understand that even “moderate” drinking is harmful - nearly double from 2015.".

7,665 likes, 45 comments - drmarkhyman on October 31, 2026: "This goes for kids and adults 😉

Halloween is one of my favorite nights of the year. The costumes, the neighborhoods, the kids running around with pure joy — there is something really special about it.

But here is what I know after 30 years of medicine: sugar on an empty stomach hits completely differently than sugar after a real meal.

Eating protein, vegetables and healthy fat before the candy reduces blood sugar spikes by up to 37%. That means less of a crash, less of a meltdown, less of a sleepless night, and more enjoyment of the actual candy because your body is not in chaos trying to handle it.

So tonight, before you head out — scrambled eggs, a piece of salmon, some roasted veggies, whatever you have. Then go have the best Halloween.

You and your kids deserve both.".

7,324 likes, 331 comments - drmarkhyman on October 30, 2026: "Lifting heavy weights may be one of the best things you can do for your brain.

A randomized controlled trial of 100,000 people found that heavy lifting, around 80% of your max for 5 to 6 reps, improved neural connectivity in the prefrontal cortex, the part of the brain that drives cognition.

Moderate weights and higher reps helped other areas of the brain. But only heavy lifting showed that prefrontal cortex response.

And it’s never too late to start. The participants were 60 and older.

Drop a YES below and I’ll DM you this full conversation with @drstacysims from The Dr. Hyman Show 🎧".

1,098 likes, 30 comments - drmarkhyman on October 28, 2026: "It’s spooky season… and PSL season. 🎃☕

But here’s what’s actually scary: a grande pumpkin spice latte has about 50 grams of sugar. That’s roughly 12 teaspoons, before you’ve even had breakfast.

When you start your day with sugar, your blood sugar shoots up fast, and then it crashes. That crash is when the brain fog, the irritability and the 10am snack attack show up. 

You grab something sweet to feel better, and the rollercoaster starts again. One sugary drink in the morning can set the tone for the rest of your day.

The fix doesn’t mean giving up fall flavors:
🍂 Add cinnamon, nutmeg and even a little pumpkin purée to your coffee
🍂 Pair it with protein and healthy fat, like eggs and avocado, to keep your energy steady

Save this for your next coffee run, and tag the friend who’s on their third PSL this week. 👇".

1,548 likes, 106 comments - drmarkhyman on October 28, 2026: "How many times have you talked yourself out of something you know is good for you in the few seconds before you act?

Bestselling author and podcast host @melrobbins explains how she created the 5 Second Rule at 41, when she was deep in debt, out of work, and struggling to get out of bed each morning. 

The moment you start counting backward from five, you’ve already decided to do the hard thing. That small, intentional action quiets the noise of your feelings and points your attention at the next step.

Tune into our full conversation to learn:

Why waiting to feel motivated keeps you stuck
How to set up your environment so the healthy choice is the easy one
The ABC method for influencing someone you love without pushing them
So much more…

Your feelings will always show up first, and learning to act anyway is where real change in your health begins.

🎧 Episode is out now. Drop a YES below and I’ll DM you the link to listen!".

2,463 likes, 79 comments - drmarkhyman on October 27, 2026: "A year and a half ago, I almost died. After back surgery, I’d lost 25 pounds and was in a wheelchair. I couldn’t walk without someone holding me up or using a walker.

I was exhausted. I was depressed. And I had to start from zero.

I didn’t feel like rebuilding my strength. I wanted to stay in bed and numb out. But with help from my physical therapist, I started with what I could manage: lying on the floor with a small resistance band around my knees, doing a few repetitions.

That was it. That was my starting point.

Then I did it again the next day.

I wanted my life back, but that didn’t mean I woke up feeling motivated to do the work. Most days, I didn’t.

If you’re starting over, I know how discouraging it can feel to remember what you used to be able to do. Start with what’s possible for you today. Let that count.".
